facts.text: On this date in 1989, the Loma Prieta earthquake struck San Francisco mid-World Series broadcast — becoming the first major US quake captured live on national television, watched by 62 million people.
On this date in 1979, Mother Teresa accepted the Nobel Peace Prize in Oslo. She declined the ceremonial banquet and asked that its $192,000 cost be given to the poor in Calcutta.
Manila is the world's most densely populated city proper, packing 111,000 people into each square kilometer — denser than any comparably sized area on Earth.
Canada has more lakes than every other country combined. Its 879,800 freshwater lakes hold about 20% of the world's total surface fresh water.

The average South Korean spends more hours per year in education and work combined than citizens of any other OECD country — yet South Korea's birth rate is the lowest ever recorded for any nation in peacetime.
On this date in 1987, global markets were three days from Black Monday — the Dow had already shed 10% the prior week, and almost nobody saw the cliff coming.
On October 17, 1973, Arab oil ministers announced their embargo against the US. The price of crude quadrupled within months, permanently ending the era of cheap energy.
The NYSE's original 1792 Buttonwood Agreement set the minimum broker commission at 0.25% — that fixed-rate cartel held, more or less, for 183 years until May Day 1975 deregulated it.
Saudi Aramco's 2019 IPO raised $25.6 billion, the largest in history — yet the company listed only 1.5% of itself, keeping the rest inside the kingdom.
The entire US bond market is roughly twice the size of the US stock market, yet most retail investors couldn't name a single bond they own.

On this date in 1967, the Outer Space Treaty entered into force — banning nuclear weapons in orbit and declaring the Moon the province of all mankind, a rule every space agency still legally operates under today.
On this date in 1604, Kepler's Supernova blazed into view — the last naked-eye supernova seen from Earth, briefly outshining every planet in the sky for over three weeks.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. One teaspoon of its matter would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Your body contains roughly 37 trillion cells, but harbors about 38 trillion bacterial cells alongside them — meaning you are, by count, slightly more microbe than human.
Light from the Sun takes eight minutes to reach Earth, but the photons themselves were generated in the solar core up to 100,000 years ago, slowly diffusing outward before finally escaping.

On this day in 1777, British General Burgoyne surrendered at Saratoga — the turning point that convinced France to back the American Revolution. The US owes its existence partly to French spite toward Britain.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. Ancient history is far stranger than the timeline feels.
On this day in 1931, Al Capone was convicted — not for murder, bootlegging, or extortion, but for tax evasion. The most feared gangster in America was felled by an accountant.
Oxford University began teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. When Montezuma was born, Oxford had already been educating scholars for 300 years.
The fax machine was invented before the telephone. You could send a document across a wire in 1843, but you couldn't speak across one until 1876.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in 'The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows,' 2012. Already feels ancient.
Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home that may never have existed. Untranslatable in one word to English, it folds grief, nostalgia, and yearning into a single exhale.
On this date in 1849, Frédéric Chopin died — and Polish gained a mourning word the world borrowed: żal, meaning grief laced with regret, sorrow aimed at something you caused yourself.
On this date in 1979, Mother Teresa received the Nobel Peace Prize. The word 'compassion' descends from Latin compati — to suffer together. She called it the rent we pay for living.

Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word from Tierra del Fuego meaning a look shared between two people, each wishing the other would initiate something both desire. One of the world's most concise observations.

On this date in 2013, Silk Road was shut down by the FBI — but its 144,000 BTC seizure sat unmoved for years, making the U.S. government one of Bitcoin's largest holders before it auctioned the coins off.

On this date in 2023, ERC-4337 account abstraction went live on Ethereum mainnet, letting smart contracts act as wallets without changing the core protocol — a decade after the idea was first proposed.
Bitcoin's timechain has never produced two consecutive blocks exactly 10 minutes apart. The 10-minute target is a probabilistic average across roughly 2,016-block difficulty windows, not a clock.
The DAO hack of 2016 drained 3.6M ETH through a reentrancy bug — but the attacker was bound by the same 28-day withdrawal lock they exploited, giving the community time to hard fork and reverse it.
Satoshi Nakamoto's known addresses have never moved a single satoshi. On-chain, the coins are provably unspent — but nothing in the protocol can prove Satoshi still holds the keys.

On this date in 2016, DeepMind's WaveNet paper was published — a generative audio model so computationally expensive it couldn't run in real time. Nine years later, its architecture underlies most production text-to-speech systems on the planet.
On this date in 2021, the Carbon Neutrality paper from Google Brain measured GPT-3's training at roughly 552 metric tons of CO2 — equivalent to driving a car to the moon and back, twice.
AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins before most structural biology labs had processed 200. The entire prior experimental record took 50 years to accumulate.

The transformer attention mechanism scales quadratically with sequence length. Every doubling of context window requires four times the compute — which is why extending from 4K to 1M tokens is not an incremental engineering step.
RLHF, the technique that made large language models feel conversational, was adapted from a 2017 robotics paper about teaching simulated agents to backflip using human preference signals.
